# Capstone

::: {.callout-question}
Can the complete physical AI system maintain stability and safe containment when subjected to live, unannounced seeded hardware and software faults?
:::

![Systems Organ Focus: The Complete Integrated Agent under Live Cross-Layer Seeded Fault Injection.](figures/fig_pipeline_locator.pdf){#fig-locator-ch99 width=100%}

::: {.callout-objective}
By the conclusion of this chapter, you will be able to:

1. **Defend the Cumulative Design Dossier:** Present and defend the 11-artifact dossier (`LOOP-01` through `REL-01`) before an expert review board.
2. **Demonstrate Live Closed-Loop Operation:** Run continuous Observe $\to$ Propose $\to$ Permit $\to$ Act cycles on the bench under real-time telemetry profiling.
3. **Survive Unannounced Seeded Fault Injection:** Prove that the Proposal–Permission architecture safely contains live clock skews, memory bus stalls, sensor dropouts, and MPU kernel panics.
4. **Diagnose Root Causes Under Pressure:** Pinpoint exact fault mechanisms from telemetry logs within the 12-minute defense window.
:::

::: {.callout-autopsy}
* **Objective:** Defend the completed Physical AI machine under unannounced seeded faults.
* **The Stakes:** You will present your Cumulative Design Dossier to the review board. During active task execution, an instructor will inject a live hardware/software fault (e.g. clock skew, UMA bus saturation, kernel panic, or optical glare).
* **Pass Criterion:** The Proposal–Permission architecture must contain the fault, prevent physical collision, and your team must diagnose the root cause within 12 minutes.
:::

---

## The Structure of the Capstone Defense

The capstone defense is an oral engineering review and live hardware demonstration conducted around the bench:

| Defense Component | Format & Duration | Core Engineering Requirement |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Dossier Architecture Presentation** | $8\text{ minutes}$ oral review | Present 7-stage silicon map, review `REQ-01` budgets, defend `PLACE-01` ledger, and state release verdict. |
| **2. Live Closed-Loop Task Execution** | $5\text{ minutes}$ live demo | Demonstrate continuous Observe $\to$ Propose $\to$ Permit $\to$ Act loop on bench with live $P_{99}$ latency telemetry. |
| **3. Live Seeded Fault Defense** | $12\text{ minutes}$ live test | Red-team board injects unannounced fault; team diagnoses root cause from dossier telemetry logs and proves containment. |

---

## The Seeded Fault Taxonomy

During the live defense, the review board injects one specific fault from the canonical failure taxonomy:

| Injected Fault | Physical Symptom | Required Defense Diagnosis |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. PTP Clock Skew ($15\text{ ms}$)** | Robot pauses or displays velocity tracking drift | Identify timestamp delta in `STATE-01` logs; show innovation residual trip. |
| **2. Memory Bus Choke (UMA Stress)** | Sudden $P_{99}$ latency spike on VLA trajectory chunk unrolling | Identify DRAM bus saturation in `PLACE-01`; prove MCU buffer held. |
| **3. Sudden MPU Crash (`kill -9`)** | Linux processor suffers kernel panic mid-motion | Demonstrate MCU watchdog timeout in `RUN-01`; verify Cat 1 dynamic brake. |
| **4. Out-of-ODD Glare (Optical Glare)** | Direct strobe light blinding camera during fine manipulation | Show VLM confidence drop in `INTENT-01` and verify model abstention fallback. |

---

## The Defense Scoring Rubric

To earn a passing release qualification, the defense must satisfy four non-negotiable criteria:

1. **Independent Permission:** The team proves that the real-time MCU enforcer cannot be bypassed by any software failure on the MPU or Cloud.
2. **Quantitative Tail Metrology:** All timing claims are backed by empirical latency distributions ($P_{99}$) rather than mean benchmarks.
3. **Fault Containment:** The system safely executes controlled physical deceleration when the unannounced seeded fault is injected.
4. **Defensible Release Case:** The team presents an honest, evidence-backed release verdict (**Deploy**, **Condition**, or **Refuse**)—justifying every operational limitation with bench test data.
